(NAFLD), refers to a wide spectrum of liver disease ranging 
from simple fatty liver (steatosis), to nonalcoholic steatohepa-
titis (NASH), to cirrhosis. Individuals who are diagnosed with
NASH tend to be middle-aged and overweight or obese (see
Chapter 12). Over 50% percent of bariatric surgery patients 
have been found to have NASH.41 Individuals with cystic ﬁ bro-
sis, an inherited disorder, have an increased risk of developing 
NASH as well (see Box 16.4).
Most patients with fatty liver are virtually asymptomatic. Hepa-
tomegaly is the most common clinical sign. Severe forms of 
fatty liver may present a clinical picture mimicking extrahepatic 
obstructive jaundice with dark urine and light stools. Typical 
abnormalities in laboratory tests are slightly or moderately 
elevated gamma glutamyltransferase (GGT) and serum trans-
